haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store, and its output goes there.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges customers and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store, and never calls the payment provider.
haiku-low.q3: Each of the last 7 consecutive days needs a mismatch rate under 0.1%, totaling at least 5,000 invoices. On-call promotes via the rollout tool, which checks the gate.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment-call failure rate exceeds 2% over 10 minutes. This applies only in both or new_only mode, not shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only once all steps are done. To move forward, on-call must promote to shadow and meet gate A from scratch.
haiku-low.q6: Rollback stops being possible 35 days after new_only began. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so the old engine's catch-up replay would be incomplete.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of each invoice. An invoice already in progress finishes under the mode it started in.
haiku-low.q8: Nightly rows in comparison_results hold the evidence. The rollout tool checks them before writing billing_mode and refuses promotions that skip a mode or fail the gate.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor measures the new engine's payment-provider call failure rate over a sliding 10-minute window. Above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Charges that fall due are written to the ledger as pending, not charged. They are charged only after resume_charging sets charging_paused to false, when the old engine charges them.
haiku-low.q11: During reconcile, an invoice already charged with matching totals is marked settled and never charged again. Mismatched totals go to the Finance review queue, not re-charged automatically.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in rolling_back with charging paused, and the new engine never resumes charging. On-call is paged, and the failed step is retried from the rollback record.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store (and never calls the payment provider).
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: each of the last 7 consecutive days has a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and together those days compared at least 5,000 invoices (only rows after the latest entry into shadow count). On-call promotes, through the rollout tool.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment-provider failure rate goes above 2% over a sliding 10-minute window. This applies in both or new_only (not shadow). It starts the rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To take over again, on-call must promote to shadow and gate A must be met from scratch (gate counts are reset).
sonnet.q6: It stops being possible 35 days after new_only began. Usage events are kept only 35 days, and catch-up needs every event since new_only began still in the log. After that the rollout tool rejects all rollbacks, manual or automatic.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of each invoice. An invoice already in progress finishes under the mode it started in.
sonnet.q8: In the comparison_results rows written nightly by the comparison job (gate B also needs a Finance sign-off recorded in the rollout tool). The rollout tool checks these rows before writing billing_mode and refuses any promotion that skips a mode or fails its gate.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the failure rate of the new engine's payment-provider calls over a sliding 10-minute window. When it goes above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Invoices that fall due are written to the ledger as pending instead of being charged (a payment call already in flight finishes). They are charged by the old engine after resume_charging sets charging_paused to false.
sonnet.q11: In reconcile, each invoice the new engine wrote is matched with the old engine's invoice for the same customer and period. If it was already charged and the totals agree, it is marked settled and never charged again. If totals differ, it goes to the Finance review queue and is not re-charged automatically.
sonnet.q12: The rollout stays in rolling_back with charging paused, and the new engine does not get charging back. On-call is paged, and the failed step is retried from the rollback record (steps are safe to repeat). Charges are delayed, not dropped or doubled.
